title: Xbox 透露 Project Helix：一台也能运行 PC 游戏的次世代主机
content:
Xbox says project Helix is a console that can play PC games
Console
Business
PC
News
Xbox teases Project Helix as 'a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC'
Xbox has revealed some more information about the upcoming console, though stops short of anything concrete or explanatory.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 16, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Image via Microsoft
As part of the Xbox 25th anniversary celebration that Microsoft's division is commemorating this week, the platform put out
a marketing-led magazine publication
about the past, present, and future of the Xbox brand, with some new information about Xbox’s next-generation console known as "Project Helix."
However, it’s not a lot of new information. In a small section teasing the device, which was
revealed earlier this year,
Xbox vice president of next generation Jason Ronald repeats a lot of previously-shared details, talks about learning lessons from the past, and stops just short of explaining exactly what the Xbox Helix is going to be.
The most relevant new revelation is that he describes the next-generation console as "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC," which is distinct from "a PC that can also play console games." Ronald then goes through great pains to communicate that the Xbox Helix is not a PC that is running a dashboard similar to a Steam Machine. Which explains what Project Helix is not, but Ronald says surprisingly little about what the next console actually is, barring a paragraph that seems to indicate that the focus is on a hybrid device.
Related:

"When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine–one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," Ronald writes. "My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games."
Erasing the wall between console and PC makes sense for Xbox, which has long shared subscription services, accounts, and even games across both Windows and Xbox. The idea of a completely open Xbox PC can likely be dismissed for now, though how exactly the platform plans to accomplish that is still a bit of a mystery.
A scant few other details are also included, such as a focus on Neural Rendering—a frame-generation technology that Ronald insists will not affect performance—along with a focus on preservation of backwards compatibility efforts both from the past and for the future. Ronald points to the ROG Xbox Ally, a handheld PC with Xbox branding and a new dashboard, as a guiding light for Project Helix.
"We view the Ally as a precursor to what we're doing with Helix—but it's informed by a lot of the design concepts we have for Helix," Ronald writes.
Back in March, newly-established Xbox announced that
development kits will start going out in 2027,
so it is likely the company will have to show its hand on Helix sooner rather than later.
